name: Maximum Projections Are Determined by the Shattered Complex
statement: Let $\Delta=\operatorname{Sh}(C)$. A coordinate set $S$ belongs to $\operatorname{MP}(C)$ exactly when $\Delta|_S$ consists of all subsets of $S$ of size at most some $d_S$. A set $S$ of size $m$ is a minimal nonface exactly when $\Delta|_S$ contains every set of size at most $m-2$ and a nonempty proper subfamily of the $(m-1)$-sets. Every corresponding bad projection needs exactly one auxiliary conditioned coordinate in a maximum parent.
proof: Projection preserves ampleness and restricts the shattered complex, so the Sauer equality gives the skeleton criterion. Exchange-connectivity of equal-size subsets shows that a minimal nonuniform restriction can mix presence and absence only in codimension one, yielding the minimal-nonface form. Complement duality turns such a projection into a rank-one maximum coordinate tree with both active and constant coordinates. Adding one auxiliary path yields a rank-one maximum parent of the complement; complementing gives the required one-auxiliary parent, while nonmaximumity excludes zero auxiliaries.
